vocab.definition: different structural forms of the same element.
a single layer of graphite — one atom thick.
carbon molecules shaped like balls or tubes.
a cylinder of carbon atoms — strong and conductive.

misconceptions.wrong: Diamond and graphite are different elements.
misconceptions.right: Both are pure carbon — just arranged differently.
Fullerenes are molecules, not giant lattices.

misconceptions.wrong: Graphene is the same as graphite.
misconceptions.right: Graphene is just one single layer of graphite.

questions.text: State what is meant by an allotrope. [1 mark]
Describe the structure of graphene. [2 marks]
Explain why graphene and nanotubes conduct electricity. [2 marks]
Suggest one use of fullerenes and why their structure suits it. [2 marks]
Complete the sentence using the word bank. [2 marks]
questions.secondaryText: Graphene is a ______ layer of carbon where each atom bonds to ______ others.

questions.text: Suggest why carbon nanotubes are used to strengthen materials. [2 marks]

footer.tip: Same element, different structure → different properties.
footer.thinkPrompt: Why does each form of carbon have a free electron except diamond?
